title: How an OpenAI influencer trip backfired
slides: Invited influencers praised OpenAI—then the backlash began.
The trip's purpose was simple: boost GPT-5 buzz.
But leaked NDAs revealed hidden strings attached.
Now creators must disclose paid ties or face fines.
Lesson: vet your influencers before they turn on you.
thread_text:
1. The hidden cost of that AI trip

OpenAI flew influencers to a lavish retreat to drum up GPT-5 hype—but the real story emerged only after leaked NDAs exposed the strings attached.

2. What the NDA actually said

Those agreements reportedly banned any negative comments for a full year. One wrong post could lead to legal action—or a hefty fine.

3. Regulators just stepped in

New FTC-style rules force creators to disclose any paid ties with AI companies. Failing that? Fines up to $40,000 per violation.

4. The backlash was brutal

Once the NDA details surfaced, influencers who praised OpenAI faced angry followers. Some deleted posts, others lost sponsors.

5. Audit your own influencer deals

Before your next campaign, ask: does my contract gag legitimate criticism? If so, rewrite it—or the public will do it for you.

instagram.caption:
A luxury retreat, a glowing post, and a 12-month gag order.

OpenAI flew influencers out to hype GPT-5, but the fine print leaked: any negative comment for a year could trigger legal action. Regulators then stepped in, and creators now face fines up to $40,000 if they don’t disclose these paid ties.

That means your next sponsored post isn't just a thumbs-up—it’s a legal contract with a muzzle attached. In fact, some influencers already deleted their praise after followers turned on them.

Before you sign your next brand deal: who owns your right to criticize—you, or the client? 🧐📝🚨
